front.title: TRAIL: Tamper-evident Records for Agent Interactions and Liveness

abstract.t: AI agents call other agents and tools across organizational boundaries, but the records of what they did are kept by the operators whose conduct the records describe, and the parties overseeing them learn of problems only afterwards. TRAIL makes this communication auditable and revocable by parties other than the operator. An enforcement point outside the agent and its sandbox, the edge, signs each call as a COSE Action Record, which the receiver keeps, and appends it to a tamper-evident trail that witnesses countersign. Authorities read the trails and publish rules that the edge enforces on every call: require approval, refuse an action, stop an agent, or cap how many agents run across machines. The edge lets traffic through only while it holds current state from each authority and a recent witness countersignature, so an authority that goes silent, or a trail that nobody is witnessing, stops the agent. TRAIL defines bindings to HTTP and to Media over QUIC Transport (MOQT) that produce the same evidence; over MOQT, holds reach edges as soon as they are published.
